newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon rates P.Telcom hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon rates P.Telcom hold.

text.p: Salomon Brothers rated Portugal Telecom as a hold saying that delay in the full liberalisation of the local telecommunications market would bring benefits.
It said in a research note that Portugal Telecom should be able to "deliver some of the best earnings growth available to telecommunications investors in Europe over the next three years."
The Portuguese telecommunications market will only be fully liberalised in 2000, putting off the impact of competitive pressures on earnings.
Salomon said that it expected the company to post net profit of 67.8 billion escudos in 1997, up from 54.9 billion last year, and pay a gross dividend of 170 escudos.

"We believe it will take some time for competition to make a serious impact in the fixed line market and Portugal Telecom's soon-to-be announced tie-up with one of the global consortia should strengthen its hold on large business customers," it said.
